a.q: Which business has a new business model that technology made possible?
opts: A firm whose app links drivers with passengers for trips
A bakery that uses an app to plan its staff rosters
A taxi firm that puts its phone number on a website
A newsagent that pays its bills with a banking app
a.why: The ride sharing firm earns its money through an app that links drivers and passengers, which is a new way of working. The bakery uses an app too, but only for rosters. It still earns money the old way, by selling bread from a shop.
a.clue: Which use of technology changes how the business earns money?

b.q: Ben sells handmade candles. He closes his market stall and sells only through a website, posting orders to buyers. Which saving is most likely?
opts: He no longer pays to rent a stall or shop
He no longer needs to make the candles
He no longer has to pay for postage
He no longer needs any customers
b.why: Selling online with no shopfront can cut the cost of renting a stall or shop. Ben still makes the candles and now pays postage. He also still needs customers.
b.clue: What cost does a business with no shopfront avoid?

flags: Question b, level: Two distractors ('He no longer needs to make the candles' and 'He no longer needs any customers') are absurd, so the question is too easy. Only the postage option is a plausible distractor.

Ride sharing
an app links a driver with a passenger who needs a trip. The business does not need to own the cars.
Online shop
sells goods over the internet and can have no shopfront. This can save the cost of renting a shop, and buyers can shop from home.
Food delivery
an app links hungry customers with restaurants and drivers. Customers can order from many restaurants in one place.

a.q: Which business is using a new business model made possible by an app?
opts: A service where an app links drivers with passengers
A bakery that sells bread from a street shop
A taxi company that takes bookings by phone only
A shop that sells paper maps to travellers
a.why: An app that links drivers with passengers is a model that relies on technology. The other three use older ways of working, such as a shop, phone bookings or paper products.
a.clue: Which one depends on an app to link buyers and sellers?

opts: He no longer pays to rent a stall or shop
He no longer needs to make the candles
He no longer has to pay for postage
He no longer needs any customers
b.why: Selling online with no shopfront can cut the cost of renting a stall or shop. Ben still makes the candles and now pays postage. He also still needs customers.

b.best: He no longer pays to rent a stall or shop

a.q: Which of these shows technology giving a business a new way to earn money?
opts: A firm whose app links drivers with riders
A bakery that plans its staff rosters with an app
A taxi firm that lists its phone number on a website
A newsagent that pays its bills through a banking app
a.why: The ride sharing firm earns its money through an app that links drivers and riders, which is a new way of working. The bakery uses an app too, but for rosters, a side task. It still earns money the old way, by selling bread from a shop.
a.clue: Which use of technology changes how the business earns money?

b.q: Ben sells handmade candles. He gives up his market stall and sells through a website instead, posting each order to the buyer. Which cost is he most likely to save?
opts: Rent for a stall at the market
Postage to send candles to buyers
Fees to keep his website running
Packing each order for posting
